answer: A shared problem bank can price identities in real work. Each epoch, an account claims one unsolved task from a public list, such as reproducing a reported bug or checking a dataset, and each task can be claimed only once. Peers grade the result before any reward unlocks. Fakes cannot share one solution: every extra account must clear its own task, terrace by terrace, so the cost rises in step with the fleet. A farm that starts at dawn with fifty names faces fifty jobs, and the delta between honest and fake effort stays near zero.
